intro: The structural multi-quarter thesis is strengthening this weekend despite the FOMC hawkish overhang. Three new developments since June 19 reinforce the long-horizon picture: (1) SK Hynix officially shipped 12-layer HBM4E samples to AI customers via SK Hynix Newsroom (48GB, 16Gbps per pin, 20%+ power efficiency) — the HBM technology roadmap is executing precisely on the schedule that supports the AI capex supercycle thesis through 2028; (2) IBIT Bitcoin ETF outflow streak ended — BlackRock's IBIT led $86M in net inflows, reversing the institutional selling signal that was the clearest post-FOMC bearish regime indicator; (3) DXY declining to ~100.23 on weekend FX confirms the Iran ceasefire Hormuz-reopening disinflation pathway is being priced by currency markets, validating the 6–10 week macro sequence (oil lower → CPI relief → Warsh dots revised → DXY peaks → rate-sensitive growth re-rates). The FOMC-driven dislocations in NVDA, META, MSFT, GOOGL, and AMZN remain multi-quarter accumulation opportunities. The structural compounder thesis — AI semis, AI memory, big-tech AI monetization, Bitcoin adoption — has not changed. Use the post-FOMC discount window while it lasts.

ideas.name: NVIDIA
ideas.idea: The toll road on AI compute — the FOMC-driven multiple discount is the structural accumulation window; SK Hynix HBM4E confirmation removes supply-chain execution risk.
ideas.why: NVDA's $25B bond raise ($85B orders, 3.4x oversubscribed) is management's public declaration of AI capex continuity regardless of the rate environment. Jensen Huang's 18-day Taiwan–South Korea trip ($150B annual spending commitment, Korean robotics/AI/memory deals) demonstrates supply-chain construction at the multi-decade horizon. The official SK Hynix HBM4E 12-layer sample shipment (48GB, 16Gbps per pin) confirms that the memory supply chain for NVDA's Vera Rubin rack-scale architecture is on schedule. The CUDA moat, Blackwell/Vera Rubin roadmap, SK Hynix supply locked through 2030, and the $299 average analyst PT create a multi-year structural bid. Warsh's hawkish dots create a near-term multiple headwind, not a change in the trajectory of AI capex. The $195–$215 zone is the structural accumulation window.
ideas.driver: Hyperscaler + sovereign AI capex compounding through 2028+; inference demand following training ramp; HBM4E supply chain execution confirmed (SK Hynix 12-layer samples); Vera Rubin rack-scale systems entering production 2026–2027; CUDA ecosystem moat expanding into robotics and physical AI.
ideas.risk: Custom ASICs (hyperscaler in-house silicon: Google TPU, AWS Trainium, Meta MTIA) erode NVDA H100/B200 share faster than expected; Fed delivers multiple 2026 hikes creating sustained 30Y above 5.25% that compresses AI-capex multiples sector-wide.

ideas.name: SK Hynix (000660.KS)
ideas.idea: 12-layer HBM4E sampling confirmed June 2026 via official Newsroom — memory AI trade entering its highest-margin product generation with the supply shortage extending through 2028 and market cap crossing ₩2,000T milestone.
ideas.why: SK Hynix's official confirmation of 12-layer HBM4E sample shipments (48GB, 16Gbps per pin, 20%+ power efficiency) is the product-cycle milestone that initiates the customer qualification process for 2027 mass production. With NVIDIA supply partnership through 2030, ~58% global HBM market share, 72% Q1 operating margin, PT revision cycle underway (consensus ₩2,690,000 already exceeded by a third consecutive session), ₩2,000T market cap milestone (passive mandate implications), potential ₩75T buyback program, and KOSPI 9,000 structural inflow bid — this is the highest-conviction structural idea in the portfolio. The AI memory shortage extending through 2028 means the pricing power in HBM4E (ASPs materially above HBM4) has a 2+ year runway. The July 29 Q2 earnings call is the next catalyst — HBM4E volume, customer qualification progress, H2 2026 margin guidance.
ideas.driver: HBM4→4E product transition with SK Hynix the clear technology leader (58% market share, 12-layer samples confirmed); shortage extending through 2028; NVIDIA supply lock; mandatory sell-side PT revision cycle from ₩2,690,000 to ₩3.0M+; KOSPI 9,000 passive inflow structural bid; potential ₩75T buyback.
ideas.risk: Samsung executes a credible HBM4E capacity ramp that captures a key NVIDIA qualification slot before SK Hynix completes customer qualification; AI capex cycle pauses in 2027 causing memory oversupply before the shortage fully resolves.

ideas.name: Microsoft
ideas.idea: The lowest-risk path to enterprise AI monetization — FOMC selloff to ~$378 is a structural accumulation opportunity in the most recurring-revenue-driven megacap.
ideas.why: Microsoft's enterprise AI thesis is compounding: Azure AI workloads are inflecting, Copilot attach rates across hundreds of millions of enterprise seats are growing, and the OpenAI investment provides asymmetric exposure to frontier model development. At ~$378, the post-FOMC selloff offers the best entry since early 2026. The recurring-revenue enterprise model makes Microsoft the least DCF-sensitive megacap to rate uncertainty — cash flows are real, current, and contracted. IBIT outflows ending and DXY declining signal the risk-on environment that drives tech re-rating, and MSFT is the safest vehicle for investors who want the recovery trade without the tail risks of NVDA (gate-dependent add) or BTC (stop-framework).
ideas.driver: Azure AI workload attach rates compounding; Copilot enterprise adoption across hundreds of millions of seats; OpenAI relationship providing frontier model access and differentiated enterprise AI capability; subscription model providing rate-insensitive cash flows.
ideas.risk: AI capex-to-Azure-revenue monetization lag extends; antitrust scrutiny of the OpenAI relationship complicates the enterprise AI bundle; new AI-native infrastructure narratives pull capital from 'mature AI' incumbents.

ideas.name: Alphabet
ideas.idea: Cheapest full-stack AI at the megacap cohort's lowest forward multiple — search cannibalization risk still priced too harshly at ~$355.
ideas.why: Alphabet owns Gemini (frontier models), TPUs (cost-competitive inference), Google Cloud (inflecting on enterprise AI), and search (generating cash for all of it). At ~$355 post-FOMC selloff, the forward multiple is the cheapest in the megacap cohort. Iran oil disinflation → lower DXY medium-term is a structural tailwind for Alphabet's emerging-market ad revenue. If AI Overviews prove to be a moat-extender (users stay on Google longer and see more premium ad inventory), the re-rating is a multi-year compounding opportunity. The TPU cost advantage in inference creates a structural pricing moat for Google Cloud AI workloads that is often underestimated relative to NVDA's ecosystem hold.
ideas.driver: TPU-driven inference cost advantage enabling competitive AI pricing; Gemini integration across billion-user surfaces; Google Cloud AI workload attach rates inflecting on enterprise adoption; potential search-moat expansion rather than cannibalization.
ideas.risk: Genuine query erosion to AI assistants at scale; antitrust remedies fracturing the search + advertising bundle; higher-for-longer rates extend the multiple compression window before the AI Overviews thesis can compound.

ideas.name: SpaceX
ideas.idea: Generational franchise; near-term step-aside after $185 stop trigger; watch for $165–$175 stabilization base + DXY below 100 before re-engaging the 3–5 year thesis.
ideas.why: SpaceX owns the only proven reusable orbital launch system at scale, Starlink at 5M+ subscribers growing ~40% annually, Starshield national-security contracts, and the AI coding platform Cursor (Anysphere, $60B stock acquisition). The June 12 IPO raised $75B at $135 — the largest ever. DXY declining to ~100.23 this weekend reduces the hawkish-rate-discount risk on the 84x revenue multiple. The near-term step-aside (stop triggered at $174.90 on June 18) is a tactical response to the FOMC hawkish repricing, not a rejection of the 3–5 year structural thesis. The structural trade: confirm stabilization at $165–$175 on June 22 with recovering volume, then hold for September 2 first earnings disclosure (Starlink subs, Cursor AI contribution, Starship revenue). December 2026 lock-up expiry ends the thin-float mechanics.
ideas.driver: Starlink subscriber and ARPU compounding toward a recurring-revenue connectivity utility (~$20B+ annualized revenue path); Starship cost-to-orbit structural reduction; Cursor AI software layer adding recurring software revenue; Starshield national-security base load.
ideas.risk: IPO-cycle overvaluation requires sustained multiple compression before traditional value investors engage at scale; September 2 first earnings disappoints vs $2.4T implied expectations; key-person concentration risk (Elon Musk); December 9 lock-up expiry is the first major supply-side event.

ideas.name: Bitcoin
ideas.idea: Structural adoption thesis intact and strengthening — IBIT outflow streak ended; DXY declining toward peak; re-entry framework at $63,500+ with improving fundamentals.
ideas.why: The IBIT outflow streak ending ($86M net inflows, BlackRock IBIT) is the clearest institutional signal that the post-FOMC BTC selling has exhausted. The structural framework — fixed supply (21M BTC hard cap), widening institutional access (IBIT, FBTC, BITA with combined $60B+ AUM), corporate treasury ownership (Strategy, MicroStrategy), halving cycle supply reduction (April 2024 most recent), and Iran ceasefire → oil lower → CPI relief → DXY peaks — is intact and strengthening with each new development. DXY declining from 100.79 to 100.23 this weekend is FX markets pricing the disinflation pathway. BTC's multi-year thesis runs on halvings and institutional access ramp, not FOMC meetings. The current $63,500–$65,000 zone is the structural accumulation window for multi-year capital.
ideas.driver: Fixed supply meeting widening institutional access (ETFs, corporate treasuries) across halving cycles; DXY structural decline as Hormuz reopening removes oil-inflation driver; IBIT inflows restarting signals institutional accumulation phase beginning; 'digital gold' narrative strengthening in a 'no forward guidance' policy regime.
ideas.risk: Warsh actually delivers multiple 2026 rate hikes (not just aspirational dots), creating a sustained DXY above 103 structurally bearish for BTC; IBIT inflow reversal proves to be short-lived (1-2 days); Strategy BTC sales signal corporate treasury accumulation thesis reversing.

ideas.name: Amazon
ideas.idea: AWS AI infrastructure winner — post-FOMC dip to ~$183 makes the entry more attractive; Hormuz reopening improves logistics economics.
ideas.why: Amazon runs the world's largest commercial cloud (AWS), is ramping Trainium/Inferentia custom silicon to reduce AI inference costs, and has a logistics-and-Prime flywheel that scales into robotic AI. The FOMC-driven selloff of ~3.46% on June 17 brought AMZN to ~$183 — the most attractive valuation point in the megacap cloud cohort. AWS AI workloads are inflecting as enterprise customers migrate to cloud-native AI. The Iran ceasefire (Hormuz reopening) reduces shipping cost inflation — a direct tailwind for Amazon's logistics economics. IBIT outflows ending + DXY declining = improving risk environment for the AWS-Prime conglomerate. The Trainium/Inferentia silicon cost advantage creates a structural pricing moat for AWS AI workloads that reduces NVDA dependency over time.
ideas.driver: AWS AI workload attach rates + Trainium/Inferentia inference cost advantage; Prime and logistics flywheel compounding at scale; Hormuz reopening reducing shipping cost inflation by 5–10% for Amazon's logistics network; AI-native robotics expansion in fulfillment centers.
ideas.risk: Cloud spending deceleration if enterprise IT budgets tighten in a higher-rate environment; competitive pressure from Azure and Google Cloud on AI workload share; Trainium/Inferentia ramp timelines extending; geopolitical risk to emerging-market logistics operations.
